messages.author: 3b9416a8eb6c69d7
messages.subject: Stan for ODE optimization
parts:
Hi to everyone,

I am completely new in Stan, reason why I write to ask for advice, opinions and suggestions.

I am working with a system of 8 coupled ordinary differential equations to model a biological fermentation process. It is a quite classic model from the point of view of theoretical biology, which as most problems in this field, counts with a considerable number of parameters (24 in total) that need to be estimated. So far, I have been working under a deterministic framework (solving the system by means of linearization which its objective is to minimize a sum of squares difference between real and simulated data). However, this approach gives me a vast uncertainty of my parameter solution space since it seems to have multiple solutions and very likely, local optimal regions.

For this reason, I was wondering if you might give me advice from your experience if such problem could be tackled with bayesian optimization using Stan. If so, what interface would you suggest me? (Rstan, PyStan?), where can I find examples of something alike (papers, websites, etc)

Any help is more than appreciated,

Waiting to hear from you soon,

Kind regards,

Mauricio

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Stan for ODE optimization
parts:
Yes.

I'd start here:

http://mc-stan.org/events/stancon2017-notebooks/stancon2017-margossian-gillespie-ode.html

and also suggest reading the manual chapter on ODEs.

Stan's modeling language is independent of Python or R, so it'll
run in both RStan and PyStan. RStan's more fleshed out and links
to auxiliary packages like ShinyStan, but both are solid interfaces
to do the basic sampling and graphing and extraction of results.

- Bob
